style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The pilgrim psalm of the sons of Korah -- temple gatekeepers by family office (1 Chronicles 9:19) -- and the Psalter's warmest love song to the house of God. It opens with an ache: soul longing to the point of fainting for the LORD's courts, heart and flesh crying out for the living God -- and then the tenderest detail in the Psalms, the sparrow and the swallow nesting beside His altars, the least of birds at home where the singer longs to be. Three beatitudes structure the psalm: blessed are those who DWELL in Your house, blessed the pilgrim whose strength is in You with the highways to Zion in his heart, and blessed -- the closing word -- simply everyone who trusts in You. The center is the pilgrimage itself: passing through the valley of Baca, the valley of weeping, they make it a place of springs, going from strength to strength until each appears before God in Zion. And the psalm's famous arithmetic settles the values question forever: one day in Your courts beats a thousand anywhere else, and the doorkeeper's threshold in the house of my God outranks residence in the tents of wickedness -- for the LORD God is a sun and shield, giving grace and glory, withholding no good thing from those who walk blamelessly.

1.text: For the choir director, on the Gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely, how beloved are Your dwelling places, O LORD of Hosts!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Gittith [gittith], A Psalm [mizmor] for the sons [ben] of Korah [Qorach]. How amiable [yedid -- how beloved, how lovely] are Your tabernacles [mishkan -- dwelling places], O LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba]!
1.notes: yedid (H3039) is the beloved-word, kin to David's own name: the mishkan (H4908) not merely admired but loved. The Korahites kept the temple doors for a living -- this is a gatekeeper's love song for the building he serves (cf. 1 Chronicles 9:19).

2.text: My soul longs -- yes, faints away -- for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out and sing toward the living God.
2.amp: My soul [nephesh] longs [kasaph -- yearns pale with longing], yea, even faints [kalah -- is consumed] for the courts [chatser] of the LORD [YHWH]: my heart [leb] and my flesh [basar] cry out [ranan -- sing aloud] for the living [chay] God [El].
2.notes: kasaph (H3700) is longing that turns the face pale, and kalah (H3615) desire consuming its own strength. leb and basar together -- the whole man, inner and outer, ranan (H7442) toward El chay: not the courts for their own sake but the living God who makes them courts (cf. Psalm 42:2).

3.text: Why, even the sparrow has found herself a home, and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young -- beside Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
3.amp: Yea, the sparrow [tsippor] has found [matsa] an house [bayith], and the swallow [deror] a nest [qen] for herself, where she may lay [shith] her young [ephroach -- her chicks], even Your altars [mizbeach], O LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba], my King [melek], and my God [Elohim].
3.notes: The smallest residents of the temple courts: tsippor and deror (H6833, H1866), nesting with their ephroach (H667) in the crannies by the mizbeach (H4196). The exile envies the birds their address -- and the titles pile up personal: my King, my God. Where the altar is, even a sparrow is home (cf. Matthew 10:29-31).

4.text: Oh the blessedness of those who dwell in Your house! They will be praising You still. Selah.
4.amp: Blessed [esher -- oh the happiness] are they that dwell [yashab] in Your house [bayith]: they will be still praising [halal] You. Selah [selah].
4.notes: First beatitude: the dwellers, the priests and gatekeepers stationed in the bayith itself, whose daily work is halal (H1984). 'Still praising' -- praise as permanent occupation, the job description of heaven begun early (cf. Revelation 7:15).

5.text: Oh the blessedness of the man whose strength is in You, in whose heart are the highways to Zion.
5.amp: Blessed [esher] is the man [adam] whose strength [oz] is in You; in whose heart [lebab] are the ways [mesillah -- the raised highways, the pilgrim roads].
5.notes: Second beatitude: not the arrived but the traveling. The mesillot (H4546) are the built-up pilgrim highways -- carried IN the lebab: the man whose inner map runs toward Zion. His oz (H5797) is in God, which matters immediately, for the road ahead runs through Baca.

6.text: Passing through the valley of Baca, the valley of weeping, they turn it into a place of springs; the autumn rain also wraps it in pools of blessing.
6.amp: Who passing [abar] through the valley [emeq] of Baca [baka -- weeping; the balsam trees], make [shith] it a well [mayan -- a spring]; the rain [moreh -- the autumn rain] also fills ['covereth', atah, the KJV margin] the pools [berakah -- blessings].
6.notes: baka (H1056) puns on weeping and names the arid balsam-tree valley: the dry, grieving stretch of every pilgrimage. The pilgrims shith (H7896), MAKE it a spring -- faith digging wells in the waste -- and heaven answers with the moreh, the early rain, until the Hebrew says the valley wears berakot (H1293), blessings, for pools.

7.text: They walk on from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.
7.amp: They go [yalak] from strength [chayil] to strength ['company to company', the KJV margin], every one of them in Zion [Tsiyyon] appears [raah] before God [Elohim].
7.notes: The pilgrim paradox: travelers should tire, these gain -- chayil (H2428) to chayil, each stage adding what it should have spent (cf. Isaiah 40:31). And the arrival is total: 'every one of them' -- no pilgrim lost in Baca -- raah before Elohim in Tsiyyon.

8.text: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; bend Your ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.
8.amp: O LORD [YHWH] God [Elohim] of hosts [tsaba], hear [shama] my prayer [tephillah]: give ear [azan], O God of Jacob [Yaaqob]. Selah [selah].
8.notes: The song pauses to become petition: shama and azan (H8085, H238), hear and bend the ear. 'God of Jacob' -- the God of the traveling schemer who met Him at Bethel on the road (cf. Genesis 28:16-17): exactly the right title for a pilgrim's prayer.

9.text: Look upon our shield, O God, and behold the face of Your anointed one.
9.amp: Behold [raah], O God [Elohim] our shield [magen], and look [nabat] upon the face [panim] of Your anointed [mashiach -- Your messiah].
9.notes: The prayer for the king: the magen (H4043) of the nation, whose panim is lifted for God's regard. mashiach (H4899) -- the anointed one -- reaches past David's line to its Heir: every pilgrim's access finally rides on the face of the Anointed being looked upon with favor (cf. Ephesians 1:6).

10.text: For one day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; I would rather stand at the threshold in the house of my God than live at ease inside the tents of wickedness.
10.amp: For a day [yom] in Your courts [chatser] is better [tov] than a thousand [eleph]. I had rather be a doorkeeper ['I would choose rather to sit at the threshold', saphaph, the KJV margin] in the house [bayith] of my God [Elohim], than to dwell [dur] in the tents [ohel] of wickedness [resha].
10.notes: The Korahite arithmetic: one yom in the chatser outvalues an eleph (H505) anywhere else. saphaph (H5605) is to stand at the sill -- the gatekeeper's own verb, the lowest post in the best house chosen over the best seat in the worst. bachar (H977), 'I would choose': values stated as a settled election.

11.text: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory. No good thing does He withhold from those who walk blamelessly.
11.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] God [Elohim] is a sun [shemesh] and shield [magen]: the LORD will give [natan] grace [chen] and glory [kabod]: no good [tov] thing will He withhold [mana] from them that walk [halak] uprightly [tamim -- blamelessly, whole].
11.notes: The only place Scripture calls God a shemesh (H8121) outright -- light, warmth, life -- balanced instantly by magen (H4043), the shade and defense: everything the pilgrim road requires. chen now, kabod (H2580, H3519) at the road's end, and the promise in between: no tov thing mana (H4513), withheld -- the pilgrim's provisioning clause (cf. Romans 8:32).

12.text: O LORD of Hosts, oh the blessedness of the man who trusts in You!
12.amp: O LORD [YHWH] of hosts [tsaba], blessed [esher] is the man [adam] that trusts [batach -- leans his whole weight] in You.
12.notes: Third beatitude, and the widest: not the dwellers only, not the pilgrims only -- simply the adam who batach (H982), leans everything on Him, wherever on the road he stands. The psalm of longing ends with blessedness available at every milepost.
